result.summary: The committed training curves say the hybrid is not "worse" than CodeBERT: it is indistinguishable from it. Every 200-epoch run (two hybrid replicates and the apparent CodeBERT-only run) has the same shape: ~10 epochs of all-positive prediction caused by inverse-frequency focal weighting, a climb to val F1@0.5 ~0.42-0.45 by epoch ~50-100, then a flat plateau to epoch 200 while probabilities polarise to {0,1} and train loss reaches ~0. Run-to-run variation at identical hyper-parameters (~2 F1 points, plots_Elevneth vs plots_12) equals the Table 1 gap (1.89). The gate curve the thesis reads as "the model progressively prioritises CodeBERT" (Figure 2 = plots_Elevneth) is not reproducible: the identical-hyper-parameter replicate flips the gate between 0/1 and 1/0 for all 200 epochs and ends at R-GCN 0.7, with the same F1; inside the thesis run itself F1 is the same whether the gate sits at R-GCN 1.0 (ep 45-72) or CodeBERT 0.8 (ep 135-200); and in plots_selfatention the same softmax gate saturated to exactly 0/1 and the network output became a constant. Fusion depth 1/3/5 changes nothing. Implication for code vs idea: the code-side problems found here (loss weighting that starts training in an all-positive regime, a threshold search that is moot once probabilities polarise, a hyper-parameter sweep run on 10% data with patience 5 under a different loss, and non-reproducible run configs) affect both arms roughly equally and do not explain the gap; the dynamics instead point to an idea/design limitation: after bidirectional cross-attention with residuals, and with graph node features that are themselves CodeBERT CLS vectors of raw code, the two "modalities" are redundant, so the gate is non-identifiable and the graph branch adds no measurable signal. Section 5.2 and the "optimisation difficulty from fusion complexity" conclusion are not supported by the student's own plots.

findings.mechanism: Before the gate, code_h and graph_h have each passed through three FusionBlocks of bidirectional cross-attention with residual+LayerNorm, so both pooled vectors v_code and v_graph are mixtures of both modalities; in addition the graph branch's node features are frozen CodeBERT CLS vectors of each node's raw code and (brief F4) the BLOCK node's CODE is the whole function body, so the 'graph' modality already contains a CodeBERT whole-function embedding. The two gated inputs are therefore near-interchangeable, the loss is flat along the gate direction, and the softmax gate drifts/saturates under optimisation noise (lr 1e-4 on the gate, no temperature or regulariser). The plotted quantity is also the epoch-mean of training-mode (dropout on) batch means, not an inference-time property. §5.2's inference and §6's 'semantic information is dominant' rest on a quantity that is not identifiable in this architecture.

findings.mechanism: Early stopping monitors F1 with patience 50 (thesis §4.4), so training runs 100+ epochs past the val-loss minimum; the weighted focal objective keeps pushing margins on the training set until all outputs saturate. The plotted train and val losses are different functions (weighted focal vs plain CE), so only their trends are comparable, but the trend is unambiguous. A saturated output distribution makes the threshold grid inert, so the claimed benefit of §4.2 is not realised at the selected checkpoints (and it would act identically on the baseline, which uses the same procedure). The polarised errors (val CE 0.15-0.2 at 97% accuracy implies per-error CE ≈ 5) also show the recall ceiling (~0.33-0.40) is set by confidently-wrong positives, not by threshold choice.

Depth neither helps nor hurts, which, together with the gate indifference in dynamics-1, says the cross-attention is not extracting complementary information from the CPG rather than that the fusion is too complex to optimise. findings.mechanism: If the graph modality carried signal complementary to CodeBERT, changing the number of cross-attention layers would change something (more capacity to exploit it, or faster overfitting). A flat response across 1-5 layers, combined with a gate whose state does not affect F1, is the signature of an input that is redundant given the other branch. That redundancy is built in: node features are frozen CodeBERT CLS vectors of raw (un-normalised, brief F4) node code, including a whole-function BLOCK node, so the R-GCN is aggregating CodeBERT embeddings over a graph whose pooled summary is close to what the fine-tuned CodeBERT branch already provides. This is a limitation of the idea as instantiated (not an optimisation bug), and it contradicts the thesis's chosen explanation that 'complexity of the fusion mechanism may introduce noise or conflicts'. Note the 1- and 5-layer runs cannot be regenerated from committed code because attn_layers is hard-coded to 3.
findings.how_to_verify: Add graph-only, random-edge and shuffled-node-feature ablations under the thesis config; if F1 is unchanged with random edges, the CPG structure contributes nothing. findings.suggested_fix: Replace node initialisation with structure-aware features that are not CodeBERT CLS of the same text (e.g. node type + token-level sub-embeddings, or a graph encoder trained from scratch), remove the whole-function BLOCK node or exclude it from pooling, and report the depth and modality ablations in the thesis.

Scope: models/LMGNN.py + models/layers.py (thesis-era f633e44 snapshot and HEAD a7122a4) vs thesis §3.3–3.5, §4.4. layers.py is byte-identical in both versions (diff = IDENTICAL); LMGNN.py differs only in BertRGCN.

(1) RECONCILIATION (thesis-era code unless noted). MATCHES: d_g=200 (era LMGNN.py:121,128-132); d_proj=200 (era:144-148, layers.py:275-276); per-relation W_r with self-loop W_0 and 1/|N_i^r| normalisation (RGCNConv default aggr='mean', root_weight=True, num_bases=None — configs.json's "aggr":"add" is never forwarded, era:130); LayerNorm only after the final R-GCN layer (era:134,186); bidirectional cross-attention Q=code/K,V=graph and Q=graph/K,V=code (layers.py:234-239); FFN + residual + post-LayerNorm after each op (layers.py:235,239,244-245); masked mean pooling (layers.py:316-332); gate = softmax(Linear(concat)) (layers.py:284,341-345); v_final = concat(a·v) (layers.py:356); CodeBERT returns token sequence L×768 (era:215-219); only last 2 encoder layers unfrozen (era:311-318); baseline = CLS (last_hidden_state[:,0], not the pooler, era:337-338) → Linear(768,200)-ReLU-Dropout(0.2)-Linear(200,2) (era:254-259); AdamW, separate CodeBERT lr via "func_encoder.bert" name match, 10% linear warmup (era run.py:1127-1161). DIFFERS: node init is 769-d = [type_id∈{0,1} from a regex on the Joern label (cpg.py:103), CLS of node code truncated to 128 tokens] (embeddings.py:47,64,182-183) vs thesis §3.3.2 "768"; "final FFN followed by a linear classifier" is actually FFN(400→800→400, no residual) → LayerNorm → Linear(400→200) → Linear(200,200)-ReLU-Dropout(0.2)-Linear(200,2) (layers.py:287-290,361-363; era:155-160); thesis-era configs.json epochs=100 vs thesis "maximum of 200 epochs"; --patience default 5 / configs 10 vs thesis 50; weight_decay hard-coded 5e-4 (configs 1.3e-6 ignored) and unreported. NOT IN THESIS: 6 R-GCN layers (configs.json:7, era:123); no residual/dropout/intermediate norm inside the R-GCN stack (era:183-184); num_bases=None; 3 fusion layers (era:152); FFN hidden 800 (=4×200, era:149); 4 heads, dropout 0.1 (era:148,151); max_length 512 (era:209); pooler left trainable but unused (590,592 params, grad is None); HEAD-only: hidden_dim overridden to 768 (HEAD LMGNN.py:138-139) and a pre-GCN node→token cross-attention + LayerNorm (HEAD:149-155,288-296).

(3) INSTANTIATION (scratch venv, CPU, real microsoft/codebert-base weights, configs.json args, Conv from layers.py; layers.py:3 os.chdir to a hard-coded path had to be patched to import). Parameters total / trainable / trainable-from-scratch(non-CodeBERT): CodeBERTOnly 124,799,834 / 14,920,538 / 154,202; thesis-era BertRGCN(200) 129,614,436 / 19,735,140 / 4,968,804 (fusion 3,812,602; rgcn 961,200; input_proj 154,000; classifier 40,602); HEAD BertRGCN(768) 196,691,716 / 86,812,420 / 72,046,084 (fusion 54,336,770; rgcn 14,160,384; context_attn 2,362,368). Each includes 14,175,744 CodeBERT last-2-layer params + 590,592 dead pooler params. Forward on a synthetic Batch of 2 graphs (5 and 7 nodes, 769-d x, 3 edge types, func strings): all three models return logits (2,2) in eval and train mode; fusion.last_weights populated (e.g. {'code':0.345,'graph':0.655}). Forward on 5 real CPG graphs from data/check_data (75/79/12/16/71 nodes) also works.

(2) OPTIMISATION PATHOLOGIES — what the evidence supports and what it does not. Supported: (a) node-input anisotropy: real frozen-CLS node features have mean pairwise cosine 0.986 (253 nodes, 5 functions), node-specific deviation 2.07 vs mean-vector norm 18.54, dim 588 ≈ 14.5±0.34 for every node and takes 57% of input_proj's gradient energy, type_id is 0.17% of input energy, mean-pooled raw features of different functions have cosine 0.9994, and nothing normalises x before input_proj (model-04); (b) the hybrid's text path is not a superset of the baseline (model-03); (c) the gate has no temperature/regulariser and the loss is scale-blind downstream, consistent with F2 saturation/flipping (model-06); (d) the §5.2 'modality weight' reading is not what the code measures (model-05). NOT supported: over-smoothing / signal attenuation in the 6-layer R-GCN stack. At random init on the real 75-node CPG, mean pairwise cosine among node vectors FALLS from 0.983 (input_proj) to ~0.75 after rgcn6 and 0.65 after rgcn_norm, norms grow (5.6→20-30), and gradient norms are flat across layers (rgcn1 5.6e-1 … rgcn6 7.2e-1; input_proj 1.95); the LayerNorm-after-concat 'undoing the gate' hypothesis reduces to the trivial fact that LN removes overall scale (|.|=19.99 for w_code 0.5/0.9/0.99) — only the ratio matters, which softmax already fixes. Capacity-vs-data (4.97M from-scratch params vs 0.15M) is plausible but the fusion-depth ablation (F3: 1/3/5 layers all ~0.40-0.42) argues against depth being decisive (model-07, low confidence).

Bottom line for the thesis question: no outright bug was found in the model files; the thesis-era architecture implements §3.4–3.5 faithfully. The negative result is better explained by implementation design choices that handicap the hybrid relative to the baseline (un-normalised near-constant graph inputs; CLS readout replaced by a from-scratch mean-pooled stack; unregularised saturating gate) plus a thesis interpretation (§5.2/§6) that the gate curve cannot support. HEAD is a different, 14× larger-from-scratch model than the one described, so the thesis cannot be reproduced from HEAD.

The over-smoothing / vanishing-signal hypothesis is therefore not supported by evidence available here; the near-constant input (model-04) is the measurable problem, not the depth.

LITERATURE VERDICT. Published evidence predicts that a *correct* implementation of "CPG graph encoder + CodeBERT fused by cross-attention" on random-split BigVul would score about the same as its own CodeBERT baseline (expected delta roughly -1 to +3 F1), with the gate drifting to the text branch. What the literature does flag as setup/code-side is the absolute level: 45.74 for a CodeBERT-class model on random-split BigVul is below every published number (54-93), which points at the recipe (last-2-layers-only, <1200-char filter, ~3% prior vs published 5.78%). And the comparison itself is under-powered: single seed, no ablation, on a dataset whose labels are 25-54% correct with 12.7% duplicates. Net: dataset/idea explains the sign (~0 gain expected), setup explains the level, and the 1.9-point gap is inside measurement noise.

findings.title: Frozen CodeBERT-CLS node features make the graph branch redundant with the text branch (contrast DeepDFA / Vul-LMGNN)
findings.claim: The thesis's node initialisation (frozen CodeBERT CLS of each node's raw code string; the BLOCK node's string is the whole function) feeds the R-GCN with text-derived summaries of the same input the fine-tuned CodeBERT branch already reads, so the graph branch adds almost no information not available to the text branch; published fusion models that report gains deliberately use node features the text encoder cannot produce (DeepDFA: abstract dataflow features excluding identifiers) or fine-tune the node encoder jointly (Vul-LMGNN). The gate converging to CodeBERT (~0.8) is the predicted equilibrium for this design, not evidence of an optimisation failure.

findings.mechanism: Every node vector is CodeBERT's CLS of a substring of the function; the BLOCK node's vector is the frozen CodeBERT CLS of the whole function, i.e. the baseline's own input representation. Message passing over AST/CFG/PDG edges then re-mixes vectors that are all projections of the same text. The only non-redundant signal is the edge topology itself, and the R-GCN must extract it through 769-d frozen text vectors. In DeepDFA the node features (API call, data type, constant, operator; top-1000 dictionary) are categorical and orthogonal to token identity, which is why concatenating them to LineVul adds information; in Vul-LMGNN the node embeddings are trainable and updated by the code LM during alternating training. Under the thesis's design the information-theoretically optimal gate weight for the graph branch is close to zero, which matches Figure 2 (0.8/0.2) and F2's gate collapse in other runs.

result.summary: Scope: dataset construction and experimental protocol (make_bigvul_json.py, select/clean/split, the sweep in run.py __main__, thesis §4-5). Bottom line for the student's question: from the data/protocol side the 43.85 vs 45.74 result cannot be read as evidence against the idea, and it also cannot be blamed on a single code bug. (1) Statistically the 1.9-point gap is inside run-to-run noise: published seed stdev of test F1 for CodeBERT/LineVul-type models is ~2.8-3.5 points (Steenhoek et al.), and the repo itself holds two hybrid runs with identical hyper-parameters whose val-F1 plateaus differ by roughly the same amount while their gate trajectories differ qualitatively; no seeds or CIs were run. (2) Several protocol defects exist but hit both models symmetrically: the FocalLoss computes p_t from the class-weighted CE so alpha enters the exponent (positives at alpha~16.7 are never down-weighted; loss on a well-classified positive is 68-238x the textbook alpha-balanced focal loss), which mis-implements §4.3 and explains the initial all-positive regime; the §4.4 grid search was run with pre-thesis code (weighted CE, 1-layer fusion, no gate), on a 10% fixed training subset with patience 5, in a regime where every config sat at val F1 ~0.15 (noise-level ranking), and the result was then handed unchanged to both the final hybrid and the baseline; whether the final runs used the full training set or the default 10% subset, and whether patience was 5, 30 or 50, is recorded nowhere. (3) The data regime is stacked against the idea before any model is trained: an undisclosed len(func)<1200-char filter keeps only functions that fit entirely into CodeBERT's 512 tokens (so the graph adds no coverage), node features are CodeBERT CLS of the same raw text, the split is a random function-level stratified split of BigVul with exact-string dedup only (literature: 54% label accuracy, 17% duplicates, 12.7% exact copies, strong leakage under random splits), and the thesis's own ~3% positive rate vs BigVul's 5.78% suggests the pipeline removed positives disproportionately. The missing ablations (graph-only, random edges, no-gate, frozen fusion) are exactly the experiments that would separate 'idea has no room on this data' from 'fusion is badly optimised'. Which code produced the thesis matters for two points: early stopping in the thesis-era code selects the checkpoint by threshold-tuned val F1 with a 1e-4 margin (HEAD uses argmax F1@0.5), and the HEAD validate() double-count (F7) is HEAD-only.

findings.claim: FocalLoss computes ce_loss with weight=alpha and then pt = exp(-ce_loss), so pt = p_t^alpha_t instead of p_t. With w1 = 0.5/0.03 = 16.7 for the vulnerable class, (1-pt)^2 is ~1 for every positive (no focusing at all), and for negatives (w0 = 0.52) pt = sqrt(p_t) so easy negatives are suppressed ~3x more than intended. The loss that is actually minimised is therefore neither the focal loss of §4.3 nor plain weighted CE; it is dominated by the ~3% positives. Identical in the thesis-era and HEAD code, and shared by both models.

result.summary: Scope: the training/validation/test/threshold loop in run.py (HEAD and the thesis-era snapshot f633e44). Verdict for the user's question: within this loop there is no defect that penalises the hybrid relative to the baseline, because both model types pass through the identical loader, criterion, optimiser grouping, scheduler, early-stopping and test-mode code. There ARE two real defects that depress both arms and make the training regime abnormal: (1) FocalLoss applies the inverse-frequency class weight inside cross_entropy before computing p_t, so the trained loss is -w_t (1 - p_t^{w_t})^2 log p_t, not thesis eq. (12); with w1 ~ 16.7 positives receive no focal damping and negatives ~4x too much, and at initialisation the gradient mass is 4.2:1 positives:negatives (vs 1:1 intended) - exactly the all-positive start (val recall 1.0, precision 0.03) visible in every training_metrics plot for both models; (2) the data stream is bit-identical every epoch (RNG re-seeded with 42+pid inside __iter__, shuffle only within 128-item windows of a sorted file list) and the default --subset_frac 0.10 trains on a fixed 10% prefix (90% of training functions never seen; whether the final runs used --no_subset is unrecorded, README:294 says yes while the sweep directories say 10%). The hybrid-vs-baseline comparison itself is statistically uninformative: one unseeded run per arm, the baseline's own validation curve (plots_codebert_first, identifiable as CodeBERTOnly by its flat-zero gate plot) is indistinguishable from the hybrid's (plateau ~0.40-0.45), the 1.89-point gap is ~1 SE of test-set sampling alone, and the (bs16, lr1e-4, ratio 0.3) configuration was selected by a patience-5, 10%-data sweep run on a pre-gating hybrid (before f633e44) and transplanted to both final models. The only hybrid-specific hazards in the loop are optimisation-setup choices, not bugs: no gradient clipping with every freshly initialised module (R-GCN, 3 fusion blocks, gate) at base_lr 1e-4 while the baseline's only fresh module is a 2-layer head (consistent with the gate flipping/collapse in F2), and a silent CUDA-OOM batch skip that only the heavier hybrid could trigger (no evidence it fired). Version dependence: HEAD's loop cannot have produced Table 1 (baseline path raises NameError, no plotting code) and it changed the selection metric from threshold-tuned val F1 (thesis-era, matching section 4.2) to F1@0.5, so only the thesis-era loop is internally consistent. Checked and found clean: optimiser param grouping ("func_encoder.bert" matches CodeBERT params in both BertRGCN and CodeBERTOnly); evaluation batch size 8 (configs.json) vs training 16 has no effect because key_padding_mask / masked mean pooling / tokenizer attention masks are used throughout; test mode treats both models identically (same loader, same threshold search on validation, same metric code); weight decay 5e-4 on LayerNorm/bias is numerically negligible (and configs.json's 1.3e-6 is not read); BalancedStreamDataset, WeightedRandomSampler and BalancedBatcher are dead code; class weights computed on the full split are fine because the subset prefix is a seed-42-shuffled random sample. Conclusion: the negative result is neither demonstrably caused by a hybrid-penalising code bug nor evidence that the idea is unsound; Table 1 cannot discriminate between those until the focal loss and the epoch-order/subset defects are fixed and seeded multi-run comparisons (with per-arm tuning) are made.

findings.title: FocalLoss applies the class weight inside cross_entropy before computing p_t, so the trained loss is -w_t(1-p_t^{w_t})^2 log p_t, not thesis eq. (12); it removes focal damping for positives, over-damps negatives, and starts training in an all-positive regime

With the inverse-frequency weights the loop builds (w0 = 0.5/0.97 = 0.516, w1 = 0.5/0.03 = 16.7 at ~3% positives), the modulating factor for a positive is (1-p^16.7)^2 >= 0.68 for all p <= 0.9 (thesis factor (1-p)^2 = 0.01 at p = 0.9), i.e. 4x-240x the eq. (12) loss, while for a negative it is 0.27-0.36x the eq. (12) factor. At initialisation (p = 0.5) the per-batch gradient mass is 4.2:1 positives:negatives, versus 1:1 under eq. (12) or under plain weighted CE.

findings.claim: order_nodes sorts by (line, col, id) with missing line numbers mapped to 10**9 (so nodes without LINE_NUMBER would be cut first), filter_nodes(strict=False) keeps nodes with empty CODE, and nodes beyond 500 are dropped. None of this matters in practice: with select() keeping only functions < 1200 chars (fact F5), the student's export of 1500 inputs has at most 288 AST nodes per method (p50 12, p90 93, p99 172, 0 over 500); in the real-pipeline sample no node lacks LINE_NUMBER/COLUMN_NUMBER and the only empty-CODE node (UNKNOWN) is removed by label. Node order does not influence the model (R-GCN, cross-attention and masked mean pooling are permutation-equivariant over nodes).
